question: True or false: patients told openly that their pills were sugar pills still reported more relief than untreated patients?
answer: True. In Ted Kaptchuk's 2010 trial, 80 people with irritable bowel syndrome got either no treatment or pills plainly labelled placebo. After three weeks, 59% of the pill group reported adequate relief, against 35% of the untreated. Ritual, attention and expectation change what a body reports, even without a lie.
move: Count the ritual and the attention as part of any treatment.
ask: Which of my daily rituals helps me mostly because of the care and attention that come with it?
trap: False, assuming a placebo works only when the patient is fooled.
reference: Kaptchuk et al., Placebos without Deception: A Randomized Controlled Trial in Irritable Bowel Syndrome, PLoS ONE 5 (12), 2010
